label: copy-phase input d (fed-back d, not first position, short sequences)
explanation: Fires almost only when the token d comes back in as input during the copy phase. 99.6% of activation mass is on copy-phase steps with input d, and it never fires in the original or delimiter phase, even on d inputs there. Most d inputs in the copy phase do not activate it (the bare predicate gets precision 0.32, recall 0.98). Which ones fire depends on position: it is silent or weak when d was the first original token (recall_idx 1), strongest for recall_idx 2-4 (the top examples are L=3-4 sequences like k d f <DEL> k [d]), and fades in long sequences (L >= 7). With repeated d (z d d o) the second d fires more weakly than the first. Rare weak activations on fed-back k/b/a/p. The refined predicate reaches dev F1 0.73 (precision 0.80, mass recall 0.86). The exact length/position dependence is smooth and is not fully captured by thresholds.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: d, k, a, p, b, r; least: 3, q, 2, 1) and the token being output (most: d, r, k, p, y, 2; least: z, v, x, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, recall_idx=3, L=3 & t=5.
